sample_unit: symptomatic patients not used for training (UCSF simulated deployment)

links.outcome: Discrimination at external safety-net site without recalibration versus development site
links.effect: Mamba AUROC 0.969 (95% CI 0.928-0.999) at UCSF and 0.965 (0.952-0.976) at ZSFG, without recalibration; median lead time 20 vs 15 months.
links.quote: Six months after presentation, among patients still undiagnosed (67% of UCSF test cases), Mamba achieved an AUROC of 0.969 (95% CI, 0.928-0.999) at UCSF and 0.965 (0.952-0.976) at ZSFG.

links.outcome: Alert burden and yield of flagged patients in simulated code-only deployment
links.effect: AUROC 0.926; reviewing 20 alerts/month identified 34 cases among 60 incident cases (PPV 1.09%, 64-fold above baseline), about one case per five months.
links.quote: Among 358,886 symptomatic patients not used for training (60 incident cases), the diagnosis-code-only model achieved an AUROC of 0.926; reviewing 20 alerts/month identified 34 cases (PPV, 1.09%; 64-fold above baseline).

screen.reason: The study develops and externally validates a longitudinal risk model for incident IBD, and evaluates simulated clinical deployment burden (measuring PPV and workload at specific alert-volume thresholds across health systems).

primary.practice: simulated deployment threshold selection and alert burden analysis
